spec.title: Round 2: the artifact script, and a name
spec.intro: Three things left from your answers. New page on purpose, so sending this does not re-send round 1.

items.title: What it actually does
items.body:
It bakes a DEAD COPY of your status board into one self-contained HTML file.

It reads three things: the wrapper's header markup, the built Punchlist app, and status-board.json. Then it welds them into a single file where the app rides in an iframe srcdoc with your tasks baked in, the active bar is frozen to whatever was active at bake time, and the graph is a static SVG drawn once.

The point was to have something shareable: a page anyone can open that shows the state of the work, with no server and no localhost. That is also exactly the problem. It strips out every line marked data-local-only and swaps the hint text to say 'Published snapshot', which tells you what it was built to be. Published.

Your own rule from 2026-07-17 then banned it: LOCAL ONLY, never publish or link artifacts, the localhost page is the artifact. So it has sat unused since, still importing the app, still reading your board.
items.placeholder: Ask if any of that is still unclear.

items.title: Three facts that should decide it
items.body:
1. It bakes your whole board into a file meant to be handed out. Every task, every note. On a public repo that is one careless command away from being a problem.

2. It is already half broken. Its graph function still looks for group-inbox and group-dir-a, the two groups your recategorization deleted, so it would bake an empty graph today. I did not fix it, because fixing a script we may delete is wasted work.

3. Deleting it costs nothing you cannot undo. It is 135 lines in git history. If you ever want a shareable snapshot again, it is one `git show` away, and honestly it would want rewriting anyway.

items.title: So: what happens to it?
items.body: My recommendation is delete. It is banned by your own rule, it is already stale, its only purpose conflicts with how you have decided to work, and it is the one file in the tool that would bake private data into a shareable page. That is a bad thing to carry into a public repo.

options: Keep it, but it stays with Punchlist, not the tool
Keep it with the tool and fix its stale graph

I have been writing agent-board in the plan and README. Whatever you pick, I will do one pass and make it consistent everywhere before we split.

items.title: Mobile group-toggle delay: I found the cause, confirm the approach
items.body: The JS is already fixed and is now a single class flip, and the hide is plain display:none with no animation. So the delay that is left is the browser laying out and painting an entire huge group the instant it opens. That is exactly why sub-item toggles feel fine to you: those subtrees are small. The native fix is one CSS property, content-visibility, which lets the browser skip work for rows that are offscreen. A group-toggle fix already shipped once and the delay survived it, so I want to measure at phone width before touching anything rather than guess a second time.

items.title: The decision the whole feature hangs on: when is a marker visible?
items.body:
Round one died on one detail. A caret at the visual end of rendered bold sits INSIDE the bold, so the code that maps your caret back to the stored text lost count, and Enter split the line in the wrong place. Pulling bold only hid it; links had it too. Any rebuild has to answer this first, and the three answers are genuinely different products.

Raw-while-editing is how Obsidian and Bear do it, and it removes the bug by construction: the row you are typing in is plain text, so there is no rendered span for a caret to hide inside.

items.title: First, what are you actually defending against?

items.title: There are only three real ways, and each costs you something
items.body:
Every device shares ONE token today, which is why forgetting cannot revoke. The three honest options:

ROTATE. Make a new token on GitHub, put it in the devices you keep, and every other device is out. Works today, costs you a trip per device you keep.

PER-DEVICE TOKENS. Each device gets its own fine-grained token, so you can kill one. Real revocation, but you create a token on GitHub for every device you ever add, forever.

A REAL LOGIN. Sign in to something instead of pasting a token. Proper revocation, and it means a server or a GitHub App, which breaks the no-server rule the whole app is built on.

items.title: The part no design can fix
items.body: A device that already synced has a full copy of your board sitting in its browser. Cutting off access stops it reading anything NEW and stops it writing. It does not reach across the internet and delete what it already has. Nothing can, short of that device opening the app again while online.

items.title: The hard constraint, stated plainly
items.body:
A reminder can only reach you if something is running when it fires. Punchlist is one HTML file with no server, so today that something is the open tab, which is why alerts only fire while the board is open.

The ways out, in order of what they cost:

CALENDAR. Scheduling writes a .ics file your real calendar swallows. Your phone then does the reminding, on the lock screen, offline, forever. Costs: the reminder lives in your calendar, so changing the time in Punchlist means re-exporting.

INSTALL IT. The hosted app becomes installable, and an installed app can wake itself to notify. Costs: only works for the hosted copy, never the file you keep on disk, and browser support for scheduled notifications is thin.

SERVER. Something of mine runs and pushes to you. Costs: the app stops being local-only, which is the thing it is.
